summary.title: Five Practical Applications of the LSTM Model for Time Series, with Code
summary.one_liner: You learn five ways to apply an LSTM neural network to time series forecasting in Python using the scalecast library: univariate, multivariate, probabilistic, dynamic probabilistic, and transfer learning.
takeaways: LSTM tends to perform better on stationary data, so detrending and de-seasonalizing before fitting can improve univariate forecasts.
Multivariate LSTM adds a related series such as price as lagged inputs; in the avocado example, transformations drove most of the accuracy.
Conformal confidence intervals from a calibration set can turn LSTM point forecasts into probabilistic forecasts that work with any ML model.
Backtesting over repeated refits lets you build dynamic intervals that widen with forecast horizon, using residuals per step.
Transfer learning with a fitted model lets you predict on new data or a related series without refitting.
summary.summary: The author revisits an earlier LSTM forecasting article and shows five practical applications using the scalecast Python library, with code and a companion notebook. Examples cover univariate forecasting on detrended air passenger data, multivariate forecasting on avocado prices and volumes with a hyperparameter grid, and probabilistic forecasting on FRED housing starts using conformal intervals. The last two sections extend this with backtesting for dynamic intervals and transfer learning to reuse a fitted model on new data or a Canadian housing series. The article is a walkthrough with reported metrics rather than a full tutorial with installation steps.
